chapter: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
title: Lyric Theatre vaudeville training and Fate Marable's invitation
summary: Zutty says his show experience came from the Lyric Theatre in New Orleans, where Willie Jackson taught him the chorus-girl steps and he bought effects. Leaving there, Fate Marable called him onto the boat, the conservatory.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, had you had much experience playing shows before?
Oh, sure. Well, I had my experience in New Orleans playing jazz shows.
That's how I got the job at the Lyric Theatre, you know, the old ______ show.

See, because Willie Jackson, who was a singer, Willie Jackson and Nookie, they used to play at a place at the Candlelight in Chicago -- I mean in New Orleans, and he'd give me steps the way the chorus girls was going to kick and go on. When he found out I was going into the Lyric Theatre. I'm going to give you an idea, Zutty, how the gals go and dance, and everything, and you --
You were sort of accents that naturally got to coincide with theirs.

That was it. I went into the Lyric Theatre, and that's where I got my vaudeville experience. I had to buy all different kind of sounds, you know, like the bell plate and it was a klaxon horn and a ratchet and things like that.
It was just grand. See that's -- when I left there that's when Fate Marable wanted me to come on the boat.
He used to say, well Zutty's going into the conservatory. See, that meant the boat, you see. Still --
